data.title: Leflunomide
data.summary: Immunomodulators · Pyrimidine synthesis inhibitor (isoxazole immunomodulator, prodrug of teriflunomide)
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Immunomodulators_

**Class:** Pyrimidine synthesis inhibitor (isoxazole immunomodulator, prodrug of teriflunomide)

## Mechanism of action
- Inhibits dihydroorotate dehydrogenase → blocks de novo pyrimidine synthesis → activated lymphocytes arrested in G1 phase

## Pharmacokinetics
- Active metabolite teriflunomide has a very long half-life (about 2 weeks) and enterohepatic recirculation — persists for up to 2 years without washout

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Psoriatic arthritis and rheumatoid arthritis (approved)
- Off-label: cutaneous/systemic lupus, Sjögren, dermatomyositis, vasculitis, sarcoidosis, BK/CMV infections in transplant

## Dose & formulations
- 10–20 mg/day (loading doses no longer routinely used)
- Washout: cholestyramine 8 g three times daily for 11 days (or activated charcoal) — before planned pregnancy or for toxicity

## Adverse effects
- Hepatotoxicity (boxed warning), diarrhoea, hypertension, weight loss, alopecia
- Cytopenias, infections, interstitial lung disease, peripheral neuropathy
- Skin: rash, SCLE induction, SJS/TEN, DRESS, cutaneous vasculitis

## Contraindications
- Pregnancy (boxed warning — teratogenic) and women not using contraception; liver disease; severe immunodeficiency

## Drug interactions
- Methotrexate (more liver toxicity), rifampicin (raises teriflunomide), cholestyramine (lowers levels), warfarin

## Monitoring
- LFT, CBC monthly for 6 months, then every 6–8 weeks; BP

## Pregnancy & lactation
Contraindicated; after stopping, washout and confirm plasma teriflunomide <0.02 mg/L on two tests before conception.

## Viva points
- DHODH inhibitor
- Cholestyramine washout because of very long half-life

_Sources: Khopkar (Leflunomide); Wolverton 4e ch.40 (Miscellaneous systemic drugs). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
